text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A day after a violent explosion in central Malmo outside a Hell's Angels motorcycle gang clubhouse, Justice Minister Laila Freivalds says she is prepared to review laws which allowed the group to buy the city centre property.
- Although jobs through temporary employement agencies offer employees higher wages than others doing the same work on a permanent basis, most would prefer regular jobs, a survey shows.
- Lithuania has agreed to purchase Bofors' Carl Gustaf grenade launcher and ammunition for $5 million, a deal the Celsius-owned defence unit is calling a breakthrough.
- Home mortgage rates are the lowest since the 1970s.
- Ferry prices across the English Channel will be unchanged after two bitter enemies, Stena Line and P&O, merge operations, Stena Line's managing director says.
- Tidnings AB Marieberg plans to start its own television channel.
- Prices on business class air tickets between Stockholm and Brussels fell nine percent in the third quarter.
- The price war between cross-channel ferry operators Swedish Stena Line and Britain's P&O is now over, with the two companies announcing they would merge operations.
- Coca-Cola has chosen Falcon brewery to be its new Swedish distributor, replacing Pripps.
- Fifty percent of Swedes will have mobile telephones by 2005, up from one in four now, a Kleinwort Benson report says.
- Building industry organisation Byggentreprenorerna says there is a small upturn ahead for the hard-hit industry.
